items.title: The radical of an ideal
Radical membership via positive powers
items.strategy: Unpack the definition of the radical and record the unit-ideal and zero-ring edge cases explicitly so later uses do not hide them.

items.title: The radical of an ideal is an ideal
items.strategy: Use the binomial theorem for sums, ideal absorption for scalar multiples, and exponent nesting for idempotence and monotonicity.

items.title: The radical of a finite intersection
items.strategy: One inclusion is immediate from monotonicity; for the reverse, raise a common product of witnessing powers into the intersection.

items.title: The radical of a product of ideals
items.strategy: Use IJ subseteq I cap J for one inclusion and multiply witnesses from sqrt(I) and sqrt(J) for the reverse.

items.title: The nilradical and reduced rings
Radicals and quotient correspondence
items.strategy: Translate power-membership in R/I back and forth across the quotient map and use the ideal correspondence theorem.

items.title: Radicals commute with localization
items.strategy: If a fraction has a power in the extended ideal, clear denominators; the forward direction is immediate from functoriality of localization.

items.title: The reduced quotient by the nilradical
items.strategy: Use the quotient-radical identification for reducedness, then factor any map to a reduced ring through the quotient by the nilradical.

items.title: A prime containing an ideal and avoiding a multiplicative set
items.strategy: Take an ideal maximal among those containing I and disjoint from S via Zorn, then prove maximal disjointness forces primality.

items.title: Separating an element from an ideal by a prime
items.strategy: Apply the multiplicative-set lemma to the powers of the chosen element.

items.title: Primes containing an ideal contain its radical
items.strategy: If a power of x lies in a prime containing I, primality removes the power one factor at a time.

items.title: A separating prime for an element outside a radical
items.strategy: If f is not in sqrt(I), no power of f lies in I, so the previous corollary produces a prime over I that omits f.

items.title: The radical of an ideal is the intersection of the prime ideals containing it
items.strategy: Combine the forward inclusion from primality with the separating-prime lemma for elements outside the radical.

items.title: The nilradical is the intersection of all prime ideals
items.strategy: Apply the radical-intersection theorem to the zero ideal.

items.title: A ring is reduced exactly when zero is an intersection of primes
items.strategy: Translate reducedness into vanishing nilradical and invoke the nilradical intersection corollary.

items.title: The prime spectrum and vanishing sets
Krull dimension of a nonzero ring
The height of a prime ideal
Vanishing sets reverse inclusions
items.strategy: A prime containing the larger ideal automatically contains the smaller one.

items.title: Vanishing sets of arbitrary sums
items.strategy: A prime contains the sum of a family exactly when it contains each summand.

items.title: Vanishing sets of finite products
items.strategy: If a prime contains a finite product of ideals, primality forces one factor ideal into the prime.

items.title: Vanishing-set identities
items.strategy: Combine the boundary cases with the arbitrary-sum and finite-product lemmas.

items.title: Vanishing sets detect radicals
items.strategy: Equal vanishing sets mean equal intersections of containing primes, hence equal radicals, and conversely radicals do not change which primes contain an ideal.

items.title: Principal distinguished subsets of the prime spectrum
Distinguished-subset identities
items.strategy: Rewrite D(f) as the complement of V(f) and use primality together with the nilradical criterion for emptiness.

items.title: Distinguished-subset covers detect radicals
items.strategy: Pass to complements and use equality of vanishing sets with equality of radicals.

items.title: The spectrum map respects composition and identities
items.strategy: Contraction of prime ideals is prime, inverse images compose, and the identity map contracts to itself.

items.title: The spectrum map pulls back vanishing sets
items.strategy: A target prime contains the extension IA exactly when its contraction contains I.

items.title: A ring map induces a contraction map on prime spectra
items.strategy: Package the contraction construction and the vanishing-set pullback lemma into the contravariant spectrum map.

items.title: Primes of a quotient lie over the kernel
items.strategy: Apply ideal correspondence and the quotient-domain criterion to transfer primality across R to R/I.

items.title: Prime ideals of a quotient ring are exactly the prime ideals containing the ideal
items.strategy: Read the quotient prime correspondence as the spectrum contraction map onto V(I).

items.title: Primes of a localization avoid the denominator set
items.strategy: Use localization ideal correspondence, checking that extension and contraction are inverse on the primes disjoint from S.

items.title: Primes of a localization at a prime
items.strategy: Specialize the localization-prime correspondence to S = R minus p.

items.title: Primes of a principal localization
items.strategy: Specialize the localization-prime correspondence to the powers of a single element.

items.title: Prime ideals of a localization are exactly the primes disjoint from the denominator set
items.strategy: Promote the localization-prime correspondence to the spectrum-level bijection.

items.title: Passing to the reduced quotient does not change the prime spectrum
items.strategy: Quotient by the nilradical and invoke the quotient-spectrum bijection together with radical detection.

items.title: Minimal primes over a proper ideal exist
items.strategy: First place the ideal inside some prime, then apply Zorn to descending chains of primes over the ideal; intersections of such chains stay prime.

items.title: The Noetherian minimal-prime induction split
items.strategy: If a radical ideal is not prime, choose x and y outside it with xy inside it and split minimal primes according to which element they contain.

items.title: The nilradical of a Noetherian ring is nilpotent
items.strategy: Use finite generation of the nilradical in a Noetherian ring and a common exponent argument for finitely many nilpotent generators.

items.title: A radical ideal in a Noetherian ring is a finite intersection of minimal primes
items.strategy: Reduce to the quotient by the radical ideal, run the Noetherian induction split there, and pull the resulting minimal primes back to R before applying the radical-intersection theorem.

items.title: A Noetherian ring has finitely many minimal prime ideals
items.strategy: Specialize the radical-ideal corollary to the zero ideal.

items.title: Height equals local dimension
items.strategy: Prime chains in R_p correspond exactly to prime chains in R ending at p, so the two suprema agree.

items.title: Dimension of a quotient via chains above an ideal
items.strategy: Translate prime chains in R/I into prime chains of R containing I by the quotient-spectrum correspondence.

items.title: The prime ideals of a field and of the integers
items.strategy: A field has only the zero ideal. For Z, prove every ideal is nZ by well-ordering, then use quotient criteria to see that nZ is prime exactly for n = 0 or n prime.

items.title: Every prime ideal of a product ring comes from one factor
items.strategy: In R x S the idempotents (1,0) and (0,1) multiply to 0, so a prime contains exactly one of them and therefore comes from one projection.

items.title: Dual numbers and their reduced quotient have the same prime set
items.strategy: Write the dual numbers as k[epsilon]/(epsilon^2); epsilon is nilpotent, so reduction identifies their prime spectra.

items.title: Minimal and maximal primes of the node ring
items.strategy: Work in k[x,y]/(xy): any prime over (xy) contains x or y, so quotient correspondence reduces the computation to the two coordinate-axis quotients and their maximal ideals.

items.title: The distinguished subset D(x) matches the primes of the localization at x
items.strategy: Primes of k[x,y]_x correspond exactly to primes of k[x,y] avoiding x, which is the distinguished subset D(x).

items.title: Computing sqrt((x^2,xy)) from its containing primes
items.strategy: Show every prime over (x^2,xy) contains x, and conversely x^2 already lies in the ideal, so the radical is (x).

items.title: A radical of a product and intersection computation
items.strategy: Compute a monomial example two ways and compare it with the product/intersection radical identities.

items.title: A separating prime for an element outside a radical
items.strategy: Use an explicit polynomial ideal and invoke the separating-prime corollary to exhibit a prime avoiding the chosen element.

items.title: The zero ring has empty prime spectrum
items.strategy: There are no proper ideals in the zero ring, so no prime ideals; then check the displayed V and D boundary cases directly.

items.title: Primes inside a localization at a prime
items.strategy: List primes below (x,y) in k[x,y], then transport them through localization at that prime.

items.title: A common nilpotence exponent in a Noetherian quotient
items.strategy: Generate the nilradical by finitely many monomials and take a common exponent guaranteed by the nilradical-nilpotence theorem.

items.title: A non-Noetherian nilradical need not be nilpotent
items.strategy: Use an infinite-variable quotient whose nilpotent generators have unbounded exponents, so no common power kills them all.
